{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.","text":"On the morning the river changed direction, Eli was the only one watching. He stood on the old footbridge with a paper bag of apples, waiting for the school bus, when the current slowed and slipped backward toward the hills.

He blinked. The water carried a yellow leaf upstream, then a twig, then a whole wooden crate. Across the river, a woman dropped her laundry basket and called for help. Eli ran to the village hall, where the mayor was setting out chairs for the harvest meeting.

“No one will believe me,” Eli said. “The river’s flowing the wrong way.”

The mayor followed him to the bridge. By then, neighbors had gathered along the bank, pointing and arguing. Old Mrs. Chen remembered a story her grandmother used to tell: when the mountain spring was blocked, the river would turn back until someone cleared its path.

The villagers fetched shovels and lanterns and followed the water toward the hills. At the narrow gorge, they found a fallen pine tree wedged between two rocks, holding back a deep pool. Together, they pushed and pulled until the trunk shifted free.

For a moment, the river stood still. Then it rushed forward with a bright, steady roar, carrying the yellow leaf toward the sea.

That evening, the harvest meeting was held beside the water. The mayor thanked Eli, but Eli was busy giving his apples to the children who had helped. He decided the strange morning had taught him something simple: noticing a problem was useful, but bringing people together could help solve it."}
